headline: Insects are Earth's dominant animals—more species, more individuals, more total mass than all other animals combined
universal_truth: Success takes many forms; what thrives isn't always what we admire
fun_facts: There are about 10 quintillion insects alive right now—that's 1.4 billion insects per human
Insects make up about 80% of all known animal species
Ants alone may weigh more than all humans combined
discussion_questions: By what measure should we judge 'success' in nature?
Why do humans rarely think of insects as the dominant life form?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: We think of lions, whales, or elephants as nature's champions. But by every objective measure—species count, population, total mass—insects dominate Earth. There are 10 quintillion insects alive right now. They're the real rulers of this planet.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Insects are tiny, short-lived, and mostly ignored by humans. Yet they've existed for 400 million years and outnumber us billions to one. What makes insects so incredibly successful?
cliff.prompt: What makes insects Earth's most successful animals?

options.text: Small size, fast reproduction, exoskeletons, flight, and incredible adaptability to diverse environments
options.response: Yes. Small means less resources needed. Fast reproduction means rapid adaptation. Flight enables escape and spread. They've optimized for survival.

options.text: They evolved before other animals and had time to spread everywhere
options.response: They are ancient, but success comes from their body plan and adaptability...

q1.title: Numbers Game
q1.script: There are about 10 quintillion individual insects alive—10 with 18 zeros after it. That's roughly 1.4 billion insects for every human. In a head count, insects win by a margin beyond comprehension.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Numbers Game"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Species Count
q2.script: About 80% of all known animal species are insects—over a million species identified, with millions more estimated to exist. For every mammal species, there are hundreds of insect species. Diversity is their kingdom.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Total Mass
q3.script: All insects together may outweigh all humans—and possibly all land vertebrates combined. Ants alone might match human mass. In sheer biomass, the tiny insects collectively outweigh the giants.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Success takes many forms. We admire size and intelligence, but insects dominate through different strategies. What thrives isn't always what we notice or admire. Nature has many ways to win.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 137. Tomorrow, we'll discover that birds are dinosaurs. Until then, notice insects around you—the true rulers of Earth.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Insect Awareness - Notice the Dominant Life Form
growTrack.learning_objective: See insects as the successful organisms they are
growTrack.activity: Look for insects today—ants, flies, beetles, bees. Remember: they outnumber you billions to one, they've existed 400 million years, and they dominate Earth by every objective measure. How does that change how you see that ant on the sidewalk?
